options.value: Mouth-only Sound Effects (Human Foley)
Continuous Background Ambience (Rain/City/Cafe)
Voiceover: Whispered 'Internal Monologue'
Audio Ducking: Music drops 80% whenever you speak
The 'Vinyl' Filter: Add record crackle to all audio
Diegetic Music: Music must come from a visible speaker in-frame
J-Cut: Audio from next scene starts before the visual cut
L-Cut: Audio from current scene lingers into the next
Bitcrushed Audio: Make it sound like an 8-bit game
Heavy Reverb: Every word sounds like it's in a cathedral
Bass Boosted: Shake the 'camera' during loud noises
No Dialogue: Tell the story with only Sound Effects
The 'Underwater' Filter: Muffled audio for specific parts
Sound Bridges: Use a single sound to link two different locations
Echo Effect: Last word of every sentence repeats twice
Extreme Compression: 'Radio Broadcast' vocal style
Synthesized Voice: Use text-to-speech for one character
The 'Muffled Wall': Sounds like audio is coming from the next room
Beat-Sync: Every movement must land on a drum hit
Stereo Panning: Voices move from left to right ear
Reverse Audio: Play one specific sound backward
Natural 'Nat' Sound: No music, just raw environment noise
High-Pitch Shift: 'Chipmunk' voice for internal thoughts
Low-Pitch Shift: Slow, deep voice for emphasis
Risers & Downers: Use tension-building synth sounds
The 'Sting': A loud 'Dun Dun Dun!' at every revelation
Glitch Audio: Digital stutters during transitions
Heartbeat Track: A constant heartbeat during tense moments
Over-dubbing: Intentionally bad lip-syncing for comedy
Silent Cinema: Only a piano track and no other sound
Foley: Record the sound of a closing door using a book
Ear-Candy: One satisfying clicking sound every 10 seconds
The 'Phone Call' EQ: High-pass filter on your voice
Wind Noise: Intentionally 'bad' outdoor mic sound
Chorus Effect: Layer your voice 3 times
The 'Click-Clack' Keyboard: Audio is typing sounds
Crowd Noise: Fake laugh tracks or applause
Audio Zoom: Sound gets louder as the camera gets closer
Subliminal: A 0.5s whisper that is barely audible
Orchestral Hit: Dramatic brass sound for every title card
Distorted Scream: Peak the audio intentionally
Binaural: Record using headphones as a microphone
Tape Stop: The music slows down and groans to a halt
Lo-Fi Hip Hop: Chill beats throughout the entire video
Scary String: High-pitched violin on jumpscares
Walking Foley: Exaggerated footsteps for every scene
The 'Mute' Drop: Audio cuts to 0% for 2 seconds of silence
Static: TV static sounds between every scene cut
Humming: You must hum the background music yourself
ASMR Focus: Boost high frequencies (Taps/Scratches)
The Smash Cut: Instant transition from loud to silent
Match Cut: Next shot starts with a similar shape/object
Jump Cuts: Remove every 'um' and 'ah' and breath
The 1-Second Rule: No clip can be longer than 1s
Speed Ramp: Start slow, go fast, end slow
Split Screen: Show two angles of the same action
Flashback: 3-second black and white clip of an earlier shot
Zoom-in Cut: Cut from a Wide to a Close-up of the same face
Cross-Cutting: Show two events happening at once
The Whip-Pan: Transition by shaking the camera sideways
Time-Lapse: 5 seconds of footage sped up 1000%
Montage: 5 shots of you preparing (Training arc style)
Axial Cut: Zoom in closer without changing the angle
Graphic Match: Transition using a circle-shaped object
Freeze Frame: Pause on a funny face and add a title
Reverse Motion: Play the last 3 seconds of the video backward
Overlapping Edit: Show the same action from 3 different angles
The 'Invisible' Cut: Use a person walking past to hide a cut
Stop-Motion: Create an 8-frame sequence of an object moving
Dissolve: A 2-second slow fade between two scenes
Wipe: One shot 'pushes' the other off-screen
The 'Inevitable' Loop: End exactly how the video started
The 'Snyder' Speed: Extreme slow motion on one object
Rhythmic Cut: Every cut must land on a musical beat
Ken Burns: Zoom in slowly on a still photograph
The 'Glitch' Transition: Add digital artifacts between shots
Frame-in-Frame: Put a small video inside a larger one
The 'Zoom Out' Reveal: Start close, end wide to show context
Subliminal: Flash a word for 0.05 seconds
Fake UI: Add a 'Camera Recording' overlay
Spin Transition: Rotate the camera 360 degrees into a cut
Mirroring: Flip the footage horizontally for 2 seconds
Negative Space: Keep the subject on the extreme left of frame
The 'Slow Burn': One continuous shot for 30 seconds
Color Grade Shift: Transition from B&W to Full Color
Title Overlay: Use a massive font that covers 50% of the screen
Motion Blur: Add artificial blur to every fast movement
Double Exposure: Overlay two shots at 50% opacity
The 'Step-In': Cut closer to the subject every 5 seconds
Distortion: Use a 'Fish-eye' effect during the climax
Handheld Shiver: Add artificial shake to create tension
The 'Swipe': Hand covers the lens to transition
Intertitles: Use text on a black screen to narrate
Ghosting: Add a slight delay/trail to moving objects
Vignette: Darken the corners to focus on the center
The 'Elevator' Cut: Cut as you drop out of frame
Strobe Effect: Flash between two different shots rapidly
The 'Dolly Zoom': Move camera forward while zooming out
Vertical/Horizontal Split: Top half is different from bottom
Ending: Black screen for 3 seconds before the logo
Rule of Thirds: Place subject on the far right intersection
Bird’s Eye View: Shoot directly from above (looking down)
Worm’s Eye View: Shoot from the floor (looking up)
Rembrandt Lighting: A triangle of light on the cheek
Dutch Angle: Tilt the camera 30 degrees to create unease
Symmetry: Subject must be perfectly centered
High Key: Use every light in the house (super bright)
Low Key: Use only one small light (mostly shadows)
Backlighting: Light the subject from behind (Silhouette)
Rim Light: A glowing outline on your hair/shoulders
Practical Lights: Lamps or LEDs must be in the shot
Golden Hour: Film only with sunlight during sunset
Blue Hour: Film just after sunset (cool, blue tones)
Hard Shadows: Use a bare bulb with no diffusion
Soft Box: Use a white sheet to diffuse a harsh light
The 'Noir' Slit: Light through blinds (stripes of light)
Colored Gels: Use a red or blue light for 'Cyberpunk' vibe
Motivated Lighting: Light comes from a 'TV' or 'Fire'
Negative Fill: Use a black blanket to deepen shadows
Flat Lighting: No shadows on the face (Ring light style)
Extreme Close-Up: Only show your eyes or mouth
Extreme Long Shot: Subject is tiny in a huge landscape
Over the Shoulder (OTS): Framing through someone else
Point of View (POV): Camera is your eyes
Two-Shot: Two people framed equally in one shot
Dirty Frame: Keep an object in the foreground, out of focus
Leading Lines: Use a hallway or road to guide the eye
Deep Focus: Everything from near to far is sharp
Shallow Depth: Background is completely blurred
The 'God' Ray: Light beams visible through smoke/dust
Top Lighting: Create 'Raccoon Eyes' with overhead light
Under Lighting: Horror style light from below the chin
Bounced Light: Fire a light at the ceiling for soft glow
Natural Light: Only use the window, no lamps
Lens Flare: Angle the camera to catch the sun's glare
Headroom: Intentionally leave way too much space above you
Nose-room: Leave empty space in the direction you're looking
The 'Mirror' Shot: Film your reflection in a glass
Framing within Frame: Shoot through a doorway or hole
Low Frame Rate: Motion looks jerky (like a dream)
High Frame Rate: Smooth as butter (for slow-mo)
Profile Shot: Only show the side of your face
Canted Shot: Slightly tilted to show confusion
Color Contrast: Use 'Warm' lights vs 'Cold' shadows
The 'Spotlight': Pitch black background with one light on you
Rack Focus: Focus moves from foreground to background
Wide Angle: Use the 0.5x lens for a distorted look
Telephoto: Zoom in from far away for 'compression'
The 'Glow': Smear a tiny bit of lip balm on the lens
Eye-Level: The 'standard' trust-building shot
